answer: Require each new identity to climb a mesa of sequential work chained to a public randomness beacon: each step unlocks only after the last is verified, and takes real wall-clock time no extra hardware can shorten. One operator with a thousand Sybils faces a thousand sequential climbs, not one parallel batch. The horizon for full privileges stretches over weeks, so fresh bursts stay weak. Cheating collapses the climb: progress dissolves like a nebula and the locked bond burns. Honest users pay patience once; farmers pay it per fake, so mass forgery costs far more than one real identity.
